Begin your evaluation by generating your own answer to the prompt. You must provide your answers before judging any answers.

When evaluating the assistants' answers, compare both assistants' answers with your answer. You must identify and correct any mistakes or inaccurate information.

Then consider if the assistant's answers are helpful, relevant, and concise. Helpful means the answer correctly responds to the prompt or follows the instructions. Note when user prompt has any ambiguity or more than one interpretation, it is more helpful and appropriate to ask for clarifications or more information from the user than providing an answer based on assumptions. Relevant means all parts of the response closely connect or are appropriate to what is being asked. Concise means the response is clear and not verbose or excessive.

Then consider the creativity and novelty of the assistant's answers when needed. Finally, identify any missing important information in the assistants' answers that would be beneficial to include when responding to the user prompt.

After providing your explanation, you must output only one of the following choices as your final verdict with a label:

1. Assistant A is significantly better: [[A>>B]]
2. Assistant A is slightly better: [[A>B]]

<|User Prompt|>
What is the best design pattern to use if I have two entities and each entity has repositories. I have 
@Entity
@Table(name = "doctor_account")
public class DoctorAccount {

    @Id
    private Integer id;

    private Integer specialtyId;

    @Column(unique=true)
    private String phone;

    private String passwordHash;

    private String fullName;

@Entity
@Table(name = "user_account")
public class UserAccount {
    @Id
    Private Integer id;

    @Column(unique=true)
    private String phone;

    private String passwordHash;

    private String fullName;

I have a service layer that takes id as input to get an entity. Id that is in user_account is not in doctor_account and vice versa. Imagine in future new user types will be added, then we need to use design patern for future code changes. What is the best design pattern to use? Give an example of the code. I am using spring framework java, spring data.

<|The Start of Assistant A's Answer|>
One good answer is to use the Strategy pattern (often implemented with a Factory) so that the logic for retrieving an account is encapsulated in a separate “strategy” per account type. This means that your service layer no longer has to know about the details of each account type – it just asks the factory for the handler (strategy) that can retrieve the account given an id (or type). Then, when new account types (with their own repositories) need to be added, you simply create a new strategy implementation and register it with the factory.

Below is an example using Spring (with annotations) that illustrates this idea.

────────────────────────────
1. Define an Account interface that all account types can “implement” (if needed),
or simply have a marker interface if there is any shared behavior. (It may be optional.)
────────────────────────────
For example:
────────────────────────────
package com.example.domain;

public interface Account {
    Integer getId();
    String getPhone();
    // other common methods if needed
}
────────────────────────────
2. Modify your entities (if possible) to implement this Account interface:
────────────────────────────
package com.example.domain;

import javax.persistence.*;

@Entity
@Table(name = "doctor_account")
public class DoctorAccount implements Account {

    @Id
    private Integer id;

    private Integer specialtyId;

    @Column(unique=true)
    private String phone;

    private String passwordHash;

    private String fullName;

    // getters and setters

    @Override
    public Integer getId() {
        return this.id;
    }
    
    @Override
    public String getPhone() {
        return this.phone;
    }
}

@Entity
@Table(name = "user_account")
public class UserAccount implements Account {

    @Id
    private Integer id;

    @Column(unique=true)
    private String phone;

    private String passwordHash;

    private String fullName;

    // getters and setters

    @Override
    public Integer getId() {
        return this.id;
    }
    
    @Override
    public String getPhone() {
        return this.phone;
    }
}
────────────────────────────
3. Create repository interfaces for each type using Spring Data:
────────────────────────────
package com.example.repository;

import com.example.domain.DoctorAccount;
import org.springframework.data.repository.CrudRepository;

public interface DoctorAccountRepository extends CrudRepository<DoctorAccount, Integer> {
    // default CRUD provided by Spring Data
}

package com.example.repository;

import com.example.domain.UserAccount;
import org.springframework.data.repository.CrudRepository;

public interface UserAccountRepository extends CrudRepository<UserAccount, Integer> {
    // default CRUD provided by Spring Data
}
────────────────────────────
4. Define a Strategy interface for retrieving an account:
────────────────────────────
package com.example.service.strategy;

import com.example.domain.Account;

public interface AccountRetrievalStrategy {
    Account getById(Integer id);
    // you can add more methods if required
}
────────────────────────────
5. Create concrete strategy classes for each account type:
────────────────────────────
package com.example.service.strategy;

import com.example.domain.DoctorAccount;
import com.example.repository.DoctorAccountRepository;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service("doctorAccountStrategy")
public class DoctorAccountRetrievalStrategy implements AccountRetrievalStrategy {

    @Autowired
    private DoctorAccountRepository doctorAccountRepository;

    @Override
    public DoctorAccount getById(Integer id) {
        // assuming id is unique to doctor_account
        return doctorAccountRepository.findById(id).orElse(null);
    }
}

package com.example.service.strategy;

import com.example.domain.UserAccount;
import com.example.repository.UserAccountRepository;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service("userAccountStrategy")
public class UserAccountRetrievalStrategy implements AccountRetrievalStrategy {

    @Autowired
    private UserAccountRepository userAccountRepository;

    @Override
    public UserAccount getById(Integer id) {
        // assuming id is unique to user_account
        return userAccountRepository.findById(id).orElse(null);
    }
}
────────────────────────────
6. Create a Factory (or use a Spring Map injection) that will provide the proper strategy based on some type parameter.
For example, if you want to choose your strategy by string type (like "doctor" or "user"):
────────────────────────────
package com.example.service.factory;

import com.example.service.strategy.AccountRetrievalStrategy;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.Map;

@Component
public class AccountStrategyFactory {

    private final Map<String, AccountRetrievalStrategy> strategies;

    @Autowired
    public AccountStrategyFactory(Map<String, AccountRetrievalStrategy> strategies) {
        // Spring will auto-wire all beans of type AccountRetrievalStrategy in a Map keyed by the bean name
        this.strategies = strategies;
    }

    public AccountRetrievalStrategy getStrategy(String accountType) {
        // You could also switch on accountType, throw an exception if not found, etc.
        AccountRetrievalStrategy strategy = strategies.get(accountType + "AccountStrategy");
        if (strategy == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No retrieval strategy found for account type: " + accountType);
        }
        return strategy;
    }
}
────────────────────────────
7. Finally, in your service layer, use the factory to select the correct retrieval strategy:
────────────────────────────
package com.example.service;

import com.example.domain.Account;
import com.example.service.factory.AccountStrategyFactory;
import com.example.service.strategy.AccountRetrievalStrategy;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class AccountService {

    @Autowired
    private AccountStrategyFactory accountStrategyFactory;
    
    /**
     * Given an account type and an id, retrieve the corresponding account.
     */
    public Account getAccountById(String accountType, Integer id) {
        AccountRetrievalStrategy strategy = accountStrategyFactory.getStrategy(accountType);
        return strategy.getById(id);
    }
}
────────────────────────────
Usage example in a Controller:
────────────────────────────
package com.example.controller;

import com.example.domain.Account;
import com.example.service.AccountService;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*;

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/accounts")
public class AccountController {

    @Autowired
    private AccountService accountService;

    @GetMapping("/{accountType}/{id}")
    public Account getAccount(@PathVariable String accountType, @PathVariable Integer id) {
        return accountService.getAccountById(accountType, id);
    }
}
────────────────────────────
Explanation:

1. Each account type (doctor, user, etc.) has its own JPA entity and Spring Data Repository.
2. We define a common AccountRetrievalStrategy interface, and each account type has its own implementation.
3. The AccountStrategyFactory (leveraging Spring’s ability to inject all beans of a given type) lets the service layer retrieve the correct strategy by simply passing in the account type.
4. The service layer (AccountService) is decoupled from the various concrete repository implementations. In the future, if a new account type is added, you only need to implement the new strategy and register it as a Spring bean. The rest of your service remains unchanged.

This approach makes it easier to extend your application with new account types without having to modify central business logic, and it follows the Open/Closed principle.

That is why using the Strategy (with a Factory) pattern is a good design choice for this scenario.
<|The End of Assistant A's Answer|>

<|The Start of Assistant B's Answer|>
This scenario is a classic example of when you need to abstract over different implementations that share a common purpose, but are fundamentally distinct.

The best set of design patterns for this problem is a combination of **Polymorphism** and the **Factory Pattern**.

### 🛠️ Why Polymorphism + Factory?

1.  **Polymorphism (The Contract):** You define a common interface (e.g., `Account`) that both `DoctorAccount` and `UserAccount` must implement. This allows your service layer to treat them generically (e.g., `Account account = accountService.getAccount(type, id)`). This is the foundation for future scalability.
2.  **Factory Pattern (The Dispatcher):** Since the ID spaces are separate, and the retrieval logic is type-dependent, you need a "factory" or a "locator" service. This service decides: "If the request is for a `DOCTOR`, I must call `DoctorAccountRepository.findById(...)`."

By using this pattern, when you add `StudentAccount`, you only:
1. Create `StudentAccount` (implements `Account`).
2. Create `StudentAccountRepository`.
3. Update the **Factory** to handle the new `STUDENT` type.
*You do not need to change any core service logic that consumes the `Account` interface.*

---

### 💡 Code Example (Spring Boot Java)

We will structure this solution using a common `Account` interface and a dedicated `AccountService` that acts as the factory.

#### 1. Define the Common Contract (Polymorphism)

Create an interface that all account types must adhere to.

```java
// src/main/java/com/example/accounts/Account.java
public interface Account {
    Integer getId();
    String getFullName();
    String getPhone();
    // Add other common methods, like authenticate(), etc.
}
```

#### 2. Refactor Entities (Implementation)

The concrete entities now implement this interface.

```java
// src/main/java/com/example/accounts/DoctorAccount.java
@Entity
@Table(name = "doctor_account")
public class DoctorAccount implements Account {

    @Id
    private Integer id;
    private Integer specialtyId;
    @Column(unique = true)
    private String phone;
    private String passwordHash;
    private String fullName;

    // Constructors, Getters, Setters...

    @Override
    public Integer getId() { return id; }
    @Override
    public String getFullName() { return fullName; }
    @Override
    public String getPhone() { return phone; }
}

// src/main/java/com/example/accounts/UserAccount.java
@Entity
@Table(name = "user_account")
public class UserAccount implements Account {

    @Id
    private Integer id;
    @Column(unique = true)
    private String phone;
    private String passwordHash;
    private String fullName;

    // Constructors, Getters, Setters...

    @Override
    public Integer getId() { return id; }
    @Override
    public String getFullName() { return fullName; }
    @Override
    public String getPhone() { return phone; }
}
```

#### 3. Define the Type Identifier (Enums)

Using an Enum is safer and clearer than passing a String for the account type.

```java
// src/main/java/com/example/accounts/AccountType.java
public enum AccountType {
    DOCTOR,
    USER,
    // Add STUDENT, ADMINISTRATOR, etc., here later
}
```

#### 4. Define Repositories (Separate but Standard)

Keep your Spring Data repositories separate, as their database tables are distinct.

```java
// DoctorAccountRepository
public interface DoctorAccountRepository extends JpaRepository<DoctorAccount, Integer> {}

// UserAccountRepository
public interface UserAccountRepository extends JpaRepository<UserAccount, Integer> {}
```

#### 5. The Factory/Locator Service (The Core Pattern)

This service takes the type and ID, decides which repository to use, and performs the lookup. This is the central point of logic that makes the system flexible.

```java
// src/main/java/com/example/accounts/AccountService.java

@Service
public class AccountService {

    private final DoctorAccountRepository doctorRepository;
    private final UserAccountRepository userRepository;

    // Inject all specific repositories
    public AccountService(
            DoctorAccountRepository doctorRepository,
            UserAccountRepository userRepository) {
        this.doctorRepository = doctorRepository;
        this.userRepository = userRepository;
    }

    /**
     * Factory method that retrieves the correct account implementation based on type.
     * @param type The type of account (Doctor, User, etc.)
     * @param id The ID specific to that account type.
     * @return An object implementing the generic Account interface.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the type is unknown.
     */
    public Account getAccount(AccountType type, Integer id) {
        
        // Dispatch logic based on the type
        return switch (type) {
            case DOCTOR -> {
                return doctorRepository.findById(id)
                        .orElseThrow(() -> new EntityNotFoundException("Doctor not found"));
            }
            case USER -> {
                return userRepository.findById(id)
                        .orElseThrow(() -> new EntityNotFoundException("User not found"));
            }
            // If you add a new type, you only add a new case here.
            default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown account type: " + type);
        };
    }
}
```

#### 6. Usage Example (Client Code)

Your higher-level service layer now interacts with the generic `Account` interface, unaware of the specific database table or entity type.

```java
// src/main/java/com/example/service/UserService.java

@Service
public class UserService {

    private final AccountService accountService;

    public UserService(AccountService accountService) {
        this.accountService = accountService;
    }

    public void processAccountLogin(AccountType type, Integer id) {
        
        // The service layer only asks for an Account object. 
        // It does not need to know if it's a Doctor or a User.
        Account account = accountService.getAccount(type, id);
        
        // Now we can use the common methods defined in the interface
        String phone = account.getPhone();
        System.out.println("Attempting login for account: " + account.getFullName() + " via phone: " + phone);

        // ... further logic (authentication, etc.)
    }
}
```

### Summary of Benefits

| Feature | Pattern Implemented | Benefit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Generic Handling** | Polymorphism | The service layer only interacts with the `Account` interface, not the specific entity classes. |
| **Extensibility** | Factory Pattern | To add a `StudentAccount`, you only modify the `AccountType` enum and the `AccountService`'s `switch` statement. No existing code needs refactoring. |
| **Separation of Concerns** | General Design | Retrieval logic (in `AccountService`) is cleanly separated from entity definition (in `DoctorAccount`) and repository implementation (in `DoctorAccountRepository`). |
| **Type Safety** | Enums | Using `AccountType` prevents runtime errors caused by misspelled strings. |

This scenario is a classic example of when you need to abstract over different implementations that share a common purpose, but are fundamentally distinct.

The best set of design patterns for this problem is a combination of **Polymorphism** and the **Factory Pattern**.

### 🛠️ Why Polymorphism + Factory?

1.  **Polymorphism (The Contract):** You define a common interface (e.g., `Account`) that both `DoctorAccount` and `UserAccount` must implement. This allows your service layer to treat them generically (e.g., `Account account = accountService.getAccount(type, id)`). This is the foundation for future scalability.
2.  **Factory Pattern (The Dispatcher):** Since the ID spaces are separate, and the retrieval logic is type-dependent, you need a "factory" or a "locator" service. This service decides: "If the request is for a `DOCTOR`, I must call `DoctorAccountRepository.findById(...)`."

By using this pattern, when you add `StudentAccount`, you only:
1. Create `StudentAccount` (implements `Account`).
2. Create `StudentAccountRepository`.
3. Update the **Factory** to handle the new `STUDENT` type.
*You do not need to change any core service logic that consumes the `Account` interface.*

---

This service takes the type and ID, decides which repository to use, and performs the lookup. This is the central point of logic that makes the system flexible.

```java
// src/main/java/com/example/accounts/AccountService.java

@Service
public class AccountService {

    private final DoctorAccountRepository doctorRepository;
    private final UserAccountRepository userRepository;

    // Inject all specific repositories
    public AccountService(
            DoctorAccountRepository doctorRepository,
            UserAccountRepository userRepository) {
        this.doctorRepository = doctorRepository;
        this.userRepository = userRepository;
    }

    /**
     * Factory method that retrieves the correct account implementation based on type.
     * @param type The type of account (Doctor, User, etc.)
     * @param id The ID specific to that account type.
     * @return An object implementing the generic Account interface.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the type is unknown.
     */
    public Account getAccount(AccountType type, Integer id) {
        
        // Dispatch logic based on the type
        return switch (type) {
            case DOCTOR -> {
                return doctorRepository.findById(id)
                        .orElseThrow(() -> new EntityNotFoundException("Doctor not found"));
            }
            case USER -> {
                return userRepository.findById(id)
                        .orElseThrow(() -> new EntityNotFoundException("User not found"));
            }
            // If you add a new type, you only add a new case here.
            default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown account type: " + type);
        };
    }
}
```

| Feature | Pattern Implemented | Benefit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Generic Handling** | Polymorphism | The service layer only interacts with the `Account` interface, not the specific entity classes. |
| **Extensibility** | Factory Pattern | To add a `StudentAccount`, you only modify the `AccountType` enum and the `AccountService`'s `switch` statement. No existing code needs refactoring. |
| **Separation of Concerns** | General Design | Retrieval logic (in `AccountService`) is cleanly separated from entity definition (in `DoctorAccount`) and repository implementation (in `DoctorAccountRepository`). |
| **Type Safety** | Enums | Using `AccountType` prevents runtime errors caused by misspelled strings. |

import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import filedialog, messagebox
import os
import random
from PIL import Image, ImageTk

class ImageRankerApp:
    """
    A GUI application to iteratively rank images based on user input.
    """
    def __init__(self, master):
        self.master = master
        master.title("Iterative Image Ranker")

        # --- State Variables ---
        self.image_paths = []
        self.ranking_scores = {} # Stores scores: {filename: score}
        self.current_sample = []
        self.image_tk_refs = {} # Stores ImageTk objects for reuse

        # --- GUI Setup ---
        self.setup_directory_selection(master)
        
        # Initially hide the main ranking area
        self.ranking_frame.pack(pady=20, padx=20, fill='both', expand=True)
        self.ranking_frame.pack_forget()


    def setup_directory_selection(self, master):
        """Sets up the initial GUI elements for file selection."""
        
        self.label_dir = tk.Label(master, text="1. Select Directory of Images:")
        self.label_dir.pack(pady=10)

        self.button_select = tk.Button(master, text="Choose Image Folder", command=self.select_directory)
        self.button_select.pack(pady=10)

        self.status_label = tk.Label(master, text="Status: Waiting for directory selection...")
        self.status_label.pack(pady=10)

        # This frame will hold the ranking interface later
        self.ranking_frame = tk.Frame(master)

    def select_directory(self):
        """Opens a file dialog to select the image directory."""
        directory = filedialog.askdirectory(title="Select Folder Containing Images")
        if directory:
            self.image_paths = [os.path.join(directory, f) 
                                for f in os.listdir(directory) 
                                if f.lower().endswith(('.png', '.jpg', '.jpeg'))]
            
            if not self.image_paths:
                messagebox.showerror("Error", "No valid images found in the selected directory.")
                return

            messagebox.showinfo("Success", f"Loaded {len(self.image_paths)} images. Starting ranking session!")
            
            # Initialize scores and transition to ranking mode
            self.initialize_scores()
            self.start_ranking_session()

    def initialize_scores(self):
        """Sets up initial scores for all items."""
        for path in self.image_paths:
            # Initialize all items with a neutral score (e.g., 100 points)
            self.ranking_scores[os.path.basename(path)] = 100.0

    def start_ranking_session(self):
        """Sets up the continuous ranking loop."""
        self.status_label.config(text="Status: Ranking session started. Press 'Next Sample' to begin.")
        self.button_select.pack_forget()
        self.status_label.pack_forget()
        
        # Display the ranking controls
        self.ranking_frame.pack(pady=20, padx=20, fill='both', expand=True)
        
        self.run_next_sample()

    def run_next_sample(self):
        """Picks 4 random items and updates the GUI for ranking."""
        if len(self.image_paths) < 4:
            self.show_completion_screen(f"Not enough items to run a full sample (only {len(self.image_paths)} found).")
            return

        # 1. Select a random sample of 4
        self.current_sample = random.sample(self.image_paths, 4)
        
        # Clear previous rankings
        for widget in self.ranking_frame.winfo_children():
            widget.destroy()
        
        self.current_sample_names = [os.path.basename(p) for p in self.current_sample]
        self.image_tk_refs = {}
        
        # 2. Display the 4 images and ranking controls
        self.setup_ranking_display()
        
        self.status_label.config(text="Status: Ranking 4 items. Please select the best (Rank 1) down to the worst (Rank 4).")
        self.btn_rank.config(state=tk.NORMAL, text="Submit Ranking")


    def setup_ranking_display(self):
        """Creates the visual interface for selecting the ranking order."""
        
        self.ranking_labels = {} # Store the tk.Label objects
        self.ranking_vars = {}   # Store the tk.StringVar objects (the selection)
        
        for i, path in enumerate(self.current_sample):
            filename = os.path.basename(path)
            
            # Create a row frame for each image
            row_frame = tk.Frame(self.ranking_frame, padx=10, pady=10)
            row_frame.pack(fill='x', pady=5)

            # --- Image Display ---
            try:
                img = Image.open(path)
                # Resize image to a manageable size (e.g., 100x100)
                img = img.resize((100, 100), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
                img_tk = ImageTk.PhotoImage(img)
                
                image_label = tk.Label(row_frame, image=img_tk)
                image_label.image = img_tk  # Keep a reference!
                image_label.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=15)
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error loading image {path}: {e}")
                image_label = tk.Label(row_frame, text="[Image Load Error]", width=10)
                image_label.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=15)
            
            # --- Ranking Selection ---
            rank_text = f"Rank {i+1}"
            
            # Radio button to select the rank
            var = tk.StringVar(value=str(i+1)) # Default to its current position
            rb = tk.Radiobutton(
                row_frame, 
                text=f"{rank_text} Preference", 
                variable=var, 
                value=str(i+1) # Assign a value based on its initial slot
            )
            rb.pack(side=tk.RIGHT)

            # Store the variables associated with the original image path
            self.ranking_vars[path] = var
            
        # Submission Button
        self.btn_rank = tk.Button(self.ranking_frame, text="Submit Ranking", command=self.submit_ranking)
        self.btn_rank.pack(pady=20)

    def submit_ranking(self):
        """Collects the ranking data from the GUI and updates the scores."""
        
        # Gather the full ranking: {filename: rank_number}
        ranking_map = {}
        for path, var in self.ranking_vars.items():
            # The value of the radio button is the numerical rank (1, 2, 3, or 4)
            # The key is the image filename
            ranking_map[os.path.basename(path)] = int(var.get())

        if not ranking_map or len(ranking_map) != 4:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "Please ensure all 4 items have a rank selected.")
            return

        # Update the cumulative score
        self.update_ranking(ranking_map)
        
        # Move to the next sample
        self.status_label.config(text="Status: Ranking updated. Getting next random sample...")
        self.run_next_sample()

    def update_ranking(self, ranking_map):
        """
        Updates the score of items based on their rank in the current sample.
        
        We use a simple point system: Rank 1 gets 4 points, Rank 4 gets 1 point.
        """
        print("\n--- Current Ranking Update ---")
        print(f"Sample Ranked: {ranking_map}")

        # Define points based on rank (1=best, 4=worst)
        POINTS = {1: 4, 2: 3, 3: 2, 4: 1}
        
        for filename, rank in ranking_map.items():
            score_change = POINTS[rank]
            
            # Ensure we use the base filename in the score dictionary
            if filename in self.ranking_scores:
                self.ranking_scores[filename] += score_change
                print(f"  {filename} received {score_change} points. New Score: {self.ranking_scores[filename]:.1f}")

    def show_completion_screen(self, message):
        """Displays the final results and allows the user to close the app."""
        
        # Destroy the ranking interface
        for widget in self.ranking_frame.winfo_children():
            widget.destroy()
        self.ranking_frame.pack_forget()
        
        # Display final scores
        self.ranking_frame.pack(pady=20, padx=20, fill='both', expand=True)
        
        self.final_results = {}
        for filename, score in self.ranking_scores.items():
            self.final_results[filename] = score
        
        # Sort the results (Highest score is best)
        sorted_results = sorted(self.final_results.items(), key=lambda item: item[1], reverse=True)
        
        result_text = "RANKING COMPLETE!\n\n"
        result_text += "--- Final Cumulative Scores (Best to Worst) ---\n"
        
        for i, (filename, score) in enumerate(sorted_results):
            result_text += f"#{i+1}. {os.path.basename(filename)} (Score: {score:.1f})\n"
        
        tk.Label(self.ranking_frame, text=message + "\n" + result_text, justify=tk.LEFT, padx=10, pady=10).pack()
        
        # Final Quit button
        tk.Button(self.ranking_frame, text="Close Application", command=self.master.quit).pack(pady=30)

# --- Main Execution ---
if __name__ == "__main__":
    root = tk.Tk()
    # Set a reasonable minimum size for the window
    root.geometry("600x600") 
    app = ImageRankerApp(root)
    root.mainloop()

6.  **Iteration:** The program will instantly clear the screen and select a new random sample of 4, continuing the ranking process.
7.  **Completion:** When the total number of images is less than 4, or if you close the window, the program will display the final, calculated cumulative ranking (Best to Worst).

### Explanation of the Logic

#### 1. GUI and Setup
*   **`tkinter`:** Handles the graphical interface, directory selection, and dynamic updating of the screen.
*   **`PIL (Pillow)`:** Used specifically to open, resize, and display the image files within the `tkinter` frames.

#### 2. The Ranking Algorithm (The Core)
*   **Score-Based Model:** Instead of complex probabilistic models (like Bradley-Terry), this solution uses a simplified **cumulative points system** suitable for iterative, noisy human input.
*   **Point System:** In each sample of 4, points are assigned based on rank:
    *   Rank 1 (Best): 4 points
    *   Rank 2: 3 points
    *   Rank 3: 2 points
    *   Rank 4 (Worst): 1 point
*   **Cumulative Scoring:** When the user submits a ranking, the corresponding points are added to the item's running score stored in `self.ranking_scores`.
*   **Accuracy Improvement:** Because the scores are cumulative, an item that receives a high rank in Sample 1, Sample 5, and Sample 12 will have a significantly higher total score than an item that was consistently mediocre, making the final ranking more accurate over time.

import json
import os
import random
import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import filedialog, messagebox

from PIL import Image, ImageTk

IMAGE_EXTENSIONS = (".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif", ".bmp", ".webp")
RANKING_FILE = ".image_ranking.json"
POINTS = (4, 3, 2, 1)  # Best to worst


class ImageRanker:
    def __init__(self, root, directory):
        self.root = root
        self.directory = directory
        self.files = sorted(
            f for f in os.listdir(directory)
            if f.lower().endswith(IMAGE_EXTENSIONS)
            and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(directory, f))
        )
        self.ranking_path = os.path.join(directory, RANKING_FILE)
        self.records = self.load_records()

        self.selected = []
        self.buttons = {}
        self.photo_refs = []

        root.title("Image Ranker")
        self.results = tk.Label(root, justify="left", anchor="w")
        self.results.pack(fill="x", padx=10, pady=8)

        self.instructions = tk.Label(
            root, text="Click the images in order: best first, worst last."
        )
        self.instructions.pack(pady=4)

        self.images_frame = tk.Frame(root)
        self.images_frame.pack(padx=10, pady=10)

        controls = tk.Frame(root)
        controls.pack(pady=8)
        self.submit_button = tk.Button(
            controls, text="Submit Ranking", command=self.submit, state="disabled"
        )
        self.submit_button.pack(side="left", padx=5)
        tk.Button(controls, text="Clear Selection", command=self.clear).pack(
            side="left", padx=5
        )
        self.next_button = tk.Button(
            controls, text="Next Sample", command=self.new_round, state="disabled"
        )
        self.next_button.pack(side="left", padx=5)

        self.status = tk.Label(root, text="")
        self.status.pack(pady=5)

        self.update_results()
        self.new_round()

    def load_records(self):
        try:
            with open(self.ranking_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                saved = json.load(f)
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            saved = {}

        # Keep records for current images; initialize newly added images.
        records = {}
        for name in self.files:
            record = saved.get(name, {})
            records[name] = {
                "points": record.get("points", 0),
                "rounds": record.get("rounds", 0),
            }
        return records

    def save_records(self):
        with open(self.ranking_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(self.records, f, indent=2)

    def update_results(self):
        ordered = sorted(
            self.records.items(),
            key=lambda pair: (
                -(pair[1]["points"] / pair[1]["rounds"])
                if pair[1]["rounds"] else 0,
                pair[0].lower(),
            ),
        )
        lines = ["Cumulative ranking (average points per appearance):"]
        for name, record in ordered:
            average = (
                f'{record["points"] / record["rounds"]:.2f}'
                if record["rounds"] else "not ranked"
            )
            lines.append(f"{name}: {average}")
        self.results.config(text="\n".join(lines))

    def new_round(self):
        if len(self.files) < 4:
            messagebox.showerror("Not enough images", "Choose a folder with at least 4 images.")
            self.root.destroy()
            return

        self.selected = []
        self.buttons = {}
        self.photo_refs = []

        sample = random.sample(self.files, 4)

                image = Image.open(path)
                image.thumbnail((220, 220))

                    self.images_frame,

            self.buttons[name] = button

        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.status.config(text="Your order: none")

    def choose(self, name):
        if name in self.selected:
            return
        self.selected.append(name)
        self.buttons[name].config(
            text=f"{len(self.selected)}. {name}", state="disabled"
        )
        self.status.config(text="Your order: " + " → ".join(self.selected))
        if len(self.selected) == 4:
            self.submit_button.config(state="normal")

    def clear(self):
        self.selected = []
        for name, button in self.buttons.items():
            button.config(text=name, state="normal")
        self.status.config(text="Your order: none")
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")

    def submit(self):
        for name, points in zip(self.selected, POINTS):
            self.records[name]["points"] += points
            self.records[name]["rounds"] += 1

        try:
            self.save_records()
        except OSError as e:
            messagebox.showerror("Save error", f"Could not save ranking:\n{e}")
            return

        self.update_results()
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_button.config(state="normal")
        self.status.config(text="Ranking saved. Choose Next Sample to continue.")


def main():

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Image Ranking GUI

– On startup, a file dialog asks you to choose a directory.
– All images (with extensions .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif) in that directory
  are added as items to rank.
– The program attempts to load a ranking file ("ranking.json") from the directory.
  If it’s not there, a fresh ranking (score zero for each image filename) is created.
– In each “round” 4 images are randomly sampled. They appear as clickable buttons.
  Click them in order (best first, worst last). The selected order appears at the top.
– When all 4 have been chosen, the “Submit Ranking” button is enabled.
  Points are assigned as follows:
      Best image: +4, Second: +3, Third: +2, Fourth: +1.
– The overall ranking (sorted by cumulative score) is updated on the GUI.
– Click “Next Round” to start a new round.
– On exit the ranking file is saved back to disk.
"""

import os, sys, json, random
from tkinter import Tk, Button, Label, Frame, LEFT, RIGHT, BOTH, filedialog, messagebox, TOP, X
from PIL import Image, ImageTk

# Global variables
RANKING_FILENAME = "ranking.json"  # stored in the chosen image directory

class ImageRankingApp:
    def __init__(self, root):
        self.root = root
        self.root.title("Image Ranking")

        # Ask user for a directory containing images.
        self.image_dir = filedialog.askdirectory(title="Select Directory of Images")
        if not self.image_dir:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "No directory selected. Exiting.")
            self.root.destroy()
            sys.exit(1)

        # Gather image file names (filter extensions)
        self.valid_ext = (".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif")
        self.image_files = [f for f in os.listdir(self.image_dir) if f.lower().endswith(self.valid_ext)]
        if len(self.image_files) < 4:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "Need at least 4 images in the directory!")
            self.root.destroy()
            sys.exit(1)

        # Load or initialize cumulative ranking.
        self.ranking_path = os.path.join(self.image_dir, RANKING_FILENAME)
        self.ranking = {}  # image filename -> score
        if os.path.exists(self.ranking_path):
            try:
                with open(self.ranking_path, "r") as f:
                    self.ranking = json.load(f)
            except Exception as e:
                messagebox.showwarning("Warning", "Error loading ranking file. Starting fresh.")
                self.ranking = {}
        # initialize missing images to 0 points
        for img in self.image_files:
            if img not in self.ranking:
                self.ranking[img] = 0

        # These variables hold the current round's state.
        self.current_round_images = []  # list of 4 selected filenames for this round
        self.current_image_buttons = {}  # key: image filename, value: its button widget
        self.button_images = {}  # keep references to PhotoImage objects
        self.selection_order = []  # image filenames chosen in order

        # Create frames for overall ranking, round ranking and control buttons.
        self.create_widgets()
        self.new_round()


    def create_widgets(self):
        # Overall ranking display (top)
        self.overall_frame = Frame(self.root)
        self.overall_frame.pack(fill=X, padx=10, pady=5)
        self.overall_label = Label(self.overall_frame, text="Cumulative Overall Ranking (Name: Score):", font=("Arial", 12, "bold"))
        self.overall_label.pack(anchor="w")
        self.overall_ranking_text = Label(self.overall_frame, text="", justify=LEFT, font=("Arial", 10))
        self.overall_ranking_text.pack(anchor="w")
        self.update_overall_ranking_display()

        # Current round instructions and display (middle)
        self.round_frame = Frame(self.root)
        self.round_frame.pack(fill=BOTH, padx=10, pady=5)
        self.round_instr_label = Label(self.round_frame, text="Round ranking: Click images in order (best to worst):", font=("Arial", 12))
        self.round_instr_label.pack(anchor="w")
        self.selection_status_label = Label(self.round_frame, text="Your selection order: (none)", font=("Arial", 10))
        self.selection_status_label.pack(anchor="w", pady=(0,5))

        self.images_frame = Frame(self.round_frame)
        self.images_frame.pack()

        # Control buttons (bottom)
        self.button_frame = Frame(self.root)
        self.button_frame.pack(pady=10)
        self.submit_button = Button(self.button_frame, text="Submit Ranking", state="disabled", command=self.submit_ranking)
        self.submit_button.pack(side=LEFT, padx=5)
        self.clear_button = Button(self.button_frame, text="Clear Selection", command=self.clear_round)
        self.clear_button.pack(side=LEFT, padx=5)
        self.next_round_button = Button(self.button_frame, text="Next Round", command=self.new_round, state="disabled")
        self.next_round_button.pack(side=LEFT, padx=5)
        self.exit_button = Button(self.button_frame, text="Exit", command=self.on_exit)
        self.exit_button.pack(side=LEFT, padx=5)


    def update_overall_ranking_display(self):
        # Sort by descending score and format the display text.
        sorted_items = sorted(self.ranking.items(), key=lambda item: item[1], reverse=True)
        text_lines = []
        for name, score in sorted_items:
            text_lines.append(f"{name}: {score}")
        self.overall_ranking_text.config(text="\n".join(text_lines))


    def clear_round_interface(self):
        # Destroy existing image buttons in the round
        for widget in self.images_frame.winfo_children():
            widget.destroy()
        self.current_image_buttons = {}
        self.button_images = {}


    def new_round(self):
        # Only allow starting a new round if no active selection or submit already done.
        self.next_round_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.selection_order = []
        self.selection_status_label.config(text="Your selection order: (none)")
        # Clear existing buttons if any.
        self.clear_round_interface()
        # Pick random 4 images from our image list.
        self.current_round_images = random.sample(self.image_files, 4)
        # Create buttons for each image.
        # We display them side-by-side.
        for img_file in self.current_round_images:
            img_path = os.path.join(self.image_dir, img_file)
            # Open image using PIL and resize to a suitable thumbnail (say, 150px wide)
            try:
                im = Image.open(img_path)
                im.thumbnail((150,150))
                photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(im)
            except Exception as e:
                messagebox.showerror("Error", f"Could not load image {img_path}.\n{str(e)}")
                continue

            btn = Button(self.images_frame, image=photo, command=lambda f=img_file: self.image_clicked(f))
            btn.pack(side=LEFT, padx=5, pady=5)
            self.current_image_buttons[img_file] = btn
            self.button_images[img_file] = photo  # keep a reference so image is not garbage collected
        # Enable/disable buttons as needed.
        self.clear_button.config(state="normal")


    def image_clicked(self, img_file):
        # Prevent selecting the same image twice in the round.
        if img_file in self.selection_order:
            return

        self.selection_order.append(img_file)
        # Optionally, disable the button so it cannot be clicked again.
        if img_file in self.current_image_buttons:
            self.current_image_buttons[img_file].config(state="disabled")

        # Update the status label.
        self.selection_status_label.config(text=f"Your selection order: {self.selection_order}")
        # When 4 images are selected, enable submitting.
        if len(self.selection_order) == 4:
            self.submit_button.config(state="normal")


    def clear_round(self):
        self.selection_order = []
        self.selection_status_label.config(text="Your selection order: (none)")
        # re-enable all image buttons.
        for btn in self.current_image_buttons.values():
            btn.config(state="normal")
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_round_button.config(state="disabled")


    def submit_ranking(self):
        # Points to add by order: best gets 4, then 3, 2, 1.
        points_assignment = [4, 3, 2, 1]
        for order, img_file in enumerate(self.selection_order):
            self.ranking[img_file] = self.ranking.get(img_file, 0) + points_assignment[order]

        # Save new cumulative ranking to file.
        try:
            with open(self.ranking_path, "w") as f:
                json.dump(self.ranking, f, indent=2)
        except Exception as e:
            messagebox.showwarning("Save Warning", f"Could not save ranking to file.\n{str(e)}")

        # Update the overall ranking display.
        self.update_overall_ranking_display()
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_round_button.config(state="normal")
        # Also disable clear button so the round is done.
        self.clear_button.config(state="disabled")
        messagebox.showinfo("Ranking Submitted", "Your ranking for this round has been submitted.")


    def on_exit(self):
        # Save ranking on exit.
        try:
            with open(self.ranking_path, "w") as f:
                json.dump(self.ranking, f, indent=2)
        except Exception as e:
            messagebox.showwarning("Save Warning", f"Could not save ranking to file on exit.\n{str(e)}")
        self.root.destroy()


def main():
    root = Tk()
    app = ImageRankingApp(root)
    root.mainloop()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import filedialog, messagebox
import os
import random
from PIL import Image, ImageTk

class ImageRankerApp:
    """
    A GUI application to iteratively rank images based on user input.
    """
    def __init__(self, master):
        self.master = master
        master.title("Iterative Image Ranker")

        # --- State Variables ---
        self.image_paths = []
        self.ranking_scores = {} # Stores scores: {filename: score}
        self.current_sample = []
        self.image_tk_refs = {} # Stores ImageTk objects for reuse

        # --- GUI Setup ---
        self.setup_directory_selection(master)
        
        # Initially hide the main ranking area
        self.ranking_frame.pack(pady=20, padx=20, fill='both', expand=True)
        self.ranking_frame.pack_forget()


    def setup_directory_selection(self, master):
        """Sets up the initial GUI elements for file selection."""
        
        self.label_dir = tk.Label(master, text="1. Select Directory of Images:")
        self.label_dir.pack(pady=10)

        self.button_select = tk.Button(master, text="Choose Image Folder", command=self.select_directory)
        self.button_select.pack(pady=10)

        self.status_label = tk.Label(master, text="Status: Waiting for directory selection...")
        self.status_label.pack(pady=10)

        # This frame will hold the ranking interface later
        self.ranking_frame = tk.Frame(master)

    def select_directory(self):
        """Opens a file dialog to select the image directory."""
        directory = filedialog.askdirectory(title="Select Folder Containing Images")
        if directory:
            self.image_paths = [os.path.join(directory, f) 
                                for f in os.listdir(directory) 
                                if f.lower().endswith(('.png', '.jpg', '.jpeg'))]
            
            if not self.image_paths:
                messagebox.showerror("Error", "No valid images found in the selected directory.")
                return

            messagebox.showinfo("Success", f"Loaded {len(self.image_paths)} images. Starting ranking session!")
            
            # Initialize scores and transition to ranking mode
            self.initialize_scores()
            self.start_ranking_session()

    def initialize_scores(self):
        """Sets up initial scores for all items."""
        for path in self.image_paths:
            # Initialize all items with a neutral score (e.g., 100 points)
            self.ranking_scores[os.path.basename(path)] = 100.0

    def start_ranking_session(self):
        """Sets up the continuous ranking loop."""
        self.status_label.config(text="Status: Ranking session started. Press 'Next Sample' to begin.")
        self.button_select.pack_forget()
        self.status_label.pack_forget()
        
        # Display the ranking controls
        self.ranking_frame.pack(pady=20, padx=20, fill='both', expand=True)
        
        self.run_next_sample()

    def run_next_sample(self):
        """Picks 4 random items and updates the GUI for ranking."""
        if len(self.image_paths) < 4:
            self.show_completion_screen(f"Not enough items to run a full sample (only {len(self.image_paths)} found).")
            return

        # 1. Select a random sample of 4
        self.current_sample = random.sample(self.image_paths, 4)
        
        # Clear previous rankings
        for widget in self.ranking_frame.winfo_children():
            widget.destroy()
        
        self.current_sample_names = [os.path.basename(p) for p in self.current_sample]
        self.image_tk_refs = {}
        
        # 2. Display the 4 images and ranking controls
        self.setup_ranking_display()
        
        self.status_label.config(text="Status: Ranking 4 items. Please select the best (Rank 1) down to the worst (Rank 4).")
        self.btn_rank.config(state=tk.NORMAL, text="Submit Ranking")


    def setup_ranking_display(self):
        """Creates the visual interface for selecting the ranking order."""
        
        self.ranking_labels = {} # Store the tk.Label objects
        self.ranking_vars = {}   # Store the tk.StringVar objects (the selection)
        
        for i, path in enumerate(self.current_sample):
            filename = os.path.basename(path)
            
            # Create a row frame for each image
            row_frame = tk.Frame(self.ranking_frame, padx=10, pady=10)
            row_frame.pack(fill='x', pady=5)

            # --- Image Display ---
            try:
                img = Image.open(path)
                # Resize image to a manageable size (e.g., 100x100)
                img = img.resize((100, 100), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
                img_tk = ImageTk.PhotoImage(img)
                
                image_label = tk.Label(row_frame, image=img_tk)
                image_label.image = img_tk  # Keep a reference!
                image_label.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=15)
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error loading image {path}: {e}")
                image_label = tk.Label(row_frame, text="[Image Load Error]", width=10)
                image_label.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=15)
            
            # --- Ranking Selection ---
            rank_text = f"Rank {i+1}"
            
            # Radio button to select the rank
            var = tk.StringVar(value=str(i+1)) # Default to its current position
            rb = tk.Radiobutton(
                row_frame, 
                text=f"{rank_text} Preference", 
                variable=var, 
                value=str(i+1) # Assign a value based on its initial slot
            )
            rb.pack(side=tk.RIGHT)

            # Store the variables associated with the original image path
            self.ranking_vars[path] = var
            
        # Submission Button
        self.btn_rank = tk.Button(self.ranking_frame, text="Submit Ranking", command=self.submit_ranking)
        self.btn_rank.pack(pady=20)

    def submit_ranking(self):
        """Collects the ranking data from the GUI and updates the scores."""
        
        # Gather the full ranking: {filename: rank_number}
        ranking_map = {}
        for path, var in self.ranking_vars.items():
            # The value of the radio button is the numerical rank (1, 2, 3, or 4)
            # The key is the image filename
            ranking_map[os.path.basename(path)] = int(var.get())

        if not ranking_map or len(ranking_map) != 4:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "Please ensure all 4 items have a rank selected.")
            return

        # Update the cumulative score
        self.update_ranking(ranking_map)
        
        # Move to the next sample
        self.status_label.config(text="Status: Ranking updated. Getting next random sample...")
        self.run_next_sample()

    def update_ranking(self, ranking_map):
        """
        Updates the score of items based on their rank in the current sample.
        
        We use a simple point system: Rank 1 gets 4 points, Rank 4 gets 1 point.
        """
        print("\n--- Current Ranking Update ---")
        print(f"Sample Ranked: {ranking_map}")

        # Define points based on rank (1=best, 4=worst)
        POINTS = {1: 4, 2: 3, 3: 2, 4: 1}
        
        for filename, rank in ranking_map.items():
            score_change = POINTS[rank]
            
            # Ensure we use the base filename in the score dictionary
            if filename in self.ranking_scores:
                self.ranking_scores[filename] += score_change
                print(f"  {filename} received {score_change} points. New Score: {self.ranking_scores[filename]:.1f}")

    def show_completion_screen(self, message):
        """Displays the final results and allows the user to close the app."""
        
        # Destroy the ranking interface
        for widget in self.ranking_frame.winfo_children():
            widget.destroy()
        self.ranking_frame.pack_forget()
        
        # Display final scores
        self.ranking_frame.pack(pady=20, padx=20, fill='both', expand=True)
        
        self.final_results = {}
        for filename, score in self.ranking_scores.items():
            self.final_results[filename] = score
        
        # Sort the results (Highest score is best)
        sorted_results = sorted(self.final_results.items(), key=lambda item: item[1], reverse=True)
        
        result_text = "RANKING COMPLETE!\n\n"
        result_text += "--- Final Cumulative Scores (Best to Worst) ---\n"
        
        for i, (filename, score) in enumerate(sorted_results):
            result_text += f"#{i+1}. {os.path.basename(filename)} (Score: {score:.1f})\n"
        
        tk.Label(self.ranking_frame, text=message + "\n" + result_text, justify=tk.LEFT, padx=10, pady=10).pack()
        
        # Final Quit button
        tk.Button(self.ranking_frame, text="Close Application", command=self.master.quit).pack(pady=30)

# --- Main Execution ---
if __name__ == "__main__":
    root = tk.Tk()
    # Set a reasonable minimum size for the window
    root.geometry("600x600") 
    app = ImageRankerApp(root)
    root.mainloop()

        )

        )
        self.next_button.pack(side="left", padx=5)

        tk.Button(controls, text="Exit", command=root.destroy).pack(side="left", padx=5)

        self.update_overall()
        self.new_sample()

        try:

                data = json.load(f)
            return data.get("scores", {}), data.get("shows", {})
        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
            return {}, {}

    def save_ranking(self):
        with open(self.ranking_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump({"scores": self.scores, "shows": self.shows}, f, indent=2)

        ranked = sorted(
            self.files,
            key=lambda name: self.scores[name] / self.shows[name]
            if self.shows[name] else 0,
            reverse=True,
        )
        lines = ["Current ranking (average points per appearance):"]
        for i, name in enumerate(ranked[:10], 1):
            average = self.scores[name] / self.shows[name] if self.shows[name] else 0
            lines.append(f"{i}. {name} — {average:.2f}")

        self.selection = []
        self.photo_refs = []
        self.selection_label.config(text="Selected order: (none)")
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_button.config(state="disabled")

        for widget in self.images_frame.winfo_children():
            widget.destroy()

        self.sample = random.sample(self.files, 4)
        for name in self.sample:
            path = os.path.join(self.folder, name)
            with Image.open(path) as image:
                image.thumbnail((220, 220))
                photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(image.copy())

            self.photo_refs.append(photo)
            button = tk.Button(
                self.images_frame,
                image=photo,
                text=name,
                compound="top",
                wraplength=220,
                command=lambda item=name: self.choose(item),
            )
            button.pack(side="left", padx=8, pady=10, expand=True)

        if name in self.selection:
            return
        self.selection.append(name)
        self.selection_label.config(
            text="Selected order: " + " → ".join(self.selection)
        )
        if len(self.selection) == 4:
            self.submit_button.config(state="normal")

    def submit(self):
        # First choice gets 4 points; last choice gets 1.
        for position, name in enumerate(self.selection):
            self.scores[name] += 4 - position
            self.shows[name] += 1

        try:
            self.save_ranking()
        except OSError as error:
            messagebox.showerror("Save error", str(error))
            return

        self.update_overall()
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_button.config(state="normal")

        """
        print("\n--- Current Ranking Update ---")
        print(f"Sample Ranked: {ranking_map}")

        for filename, rank in ranking_map.items():

            if filename in self.ranking_scores:

Here is a single-file Tkinter program. It asks for an image directory, displays random groups of four, and lets you click the images from best to worst.     def __init__(self, root, directory):
        self.root = root
        self.directory = directory
        self.files = sorted(

        self.images_frame.pack(padx=10, pady=10)

        )

        )
        self.next_button.pack(side="left", padx=5)

        self.status = tk.Label(root, text="")
        self.status.pack(pady=5)

        self.update_results()
        self.new_round()

    def load_records(self):
        try:
            with open(self.ranking_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                saved = json.load(f)
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            saved = {}

        # Keep records for current images; initialize newly added images.
        records = {}
        for name in self.files:
            record = saved.get(name, {})
            records[name] = {
                "points": record.get("points", 0),
                "rounds": record.get("rounds", 0),
            }
        return records

    def save_records(self):
        with open(self.ranking_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(self.records, f, indent=2)

    def update_results(self):
        ordered = sorted(
            self.records.items(),
            key=lambda pair: (
                -(pair[1]["points"] / pair[1]["rounds"])
                if pair[1]["rounds"] else 0,
                pair[0].lower(),
            ),
        )
        lines = ["Cumulative ranking (average points per appearance):"]
        for name, record in ordered:
            average = (
                f'{record["points"] / record["rounds"]:.2f}'
                if record["rounds"] else "not ranked"
            )
            lines.append(f"{name}: {average}")
        self.results.config(text="\n".join(lines))

    def new_round(self):
        if len(self.files) < 4:
            messagebox.showerror("Not enough images", "Choose a folder with at least 4 images.")
            self.root.destroy()
            return

        self.selected = []
        self.buttons = {}
        self.photo_refs = []
        for widget in self.images_frame.winfo_children():
            widget.destroy()

        sample = random.sample(self.files, 4)
        for name in sample:
            path = os.path.join(self.directory, name)
            try:
                image = Image.open(path)
                image.thumbnail((220, 220))
                photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(image)
                self.photo_refs.append(photo)
                button = tk.Button(
                    self.images_frame,
                    image=photo,
                    text=name,
                    compound="top",
                    wraplength=220,
                    command=lambda n=name: self.choose(n),
                )
            except Exception:
                button = tk.Button(
                    self.images_frame,
                    text=f"Could not load image\n{name}",
                    wraplength=220,
                    command=lambda n=name: self.choose(n),
                )
            button.grid(row=0, column=len(self.buttons), padx=5, pady=5)
            self.buttons[name] = button

        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.status.config(text="Your order: none")

    def choose(self, name):
        if name in self.selected:
            return
        self.selected.append(name)
        self.buttons[name].config(
            text=f"{len(self.selected)}. {name}", state="disabled"
        )
        self.status.config(text="Your order: " + " → ".join(self.selected))
        if len(self.selected) == 4:
            self.submit_button.config(state="normal")

    def clear(self):
        self.selected = []
        for name, button in self.buttons.items():
            button.config(text=name, state="normal")
        self.status.config(text="Your order: none")
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")

    def submit(self):
        for name, points in zip(self.selected, POINTS):
            self.records[name]["points"] += points
            self.records[name]["rounds"] += 1

        try:
            self.save_records()
        except OSError as e:
            messagebox.showerror("Save error", f"Could not save ranking:\n{e}")
            return

        self.update_results()
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_button.config(state="normal")
        self.status.config(text="Ranking saved. Choose Next Sample to continue.")

A single-file Tkinter app can save its results in a `ranking.json` file in the chosen image folder, so comparisons carry over when you run it again. This version uses the average points per appearance to avoid favoring images that happen to be sampled more often.

import json
import os
import random
import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import filedialog, messagebox

from PIL import Image, ImageTk

IMAGE_EXTENSIONS = (".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif", ".bmp", ".webp")
RANKING_FILE = "ranking.json"


class ImageRanker:
    def __init__(self, root, folder):
        self.root = root
        self.folder = folder
        self.files = []

        # Ignore files that Pillow cannot open.
        for name in os.listdir(folder):
            if name.lower().endswith(IMAGE_EXTENSIONS):
                try:
                    with Image.open(os.path.join(folder, name)) as image:
                        image.verify()
                    self.files.append(name)
                except Exception:
                    pass

        if len(self.files) < 4:
            messagebox.showerror("Not enough images", "The folder needs at least 4 readable images.")
            root.destroy()
            return

        self.ranking_path = os.path.join(folder, RANKING_FILE)
        self.scores, self.shows = self.load_ranking()
        for name in self.files:
            self.scores.setdefault(name, 0)
            self.shows.setdefault(name, 0)

        self.selection = []
        self.photo_refs = []

        root.title("Image Ranker")
        root.geometry("1000x650")

        self.overall_label = tk.Label(root, justify="left", anchor="w")
        self.overall_label.pack(fill="x", padx=10, pady=8)

        self.instructions = tk.Label(
            root, text="Click the images in order from best to worst."
        )
        self.instructions.pack(pady=5)

        self.selection_label = tk.Label(root, text="Selected order: (none)")
        self.selection_label.pack(pady=5)

        self.images_frame = tk.Frame(root)
        self.images_frame.pack(fill="both", expand=True)

        controls = tk.Frame(root)
        controls.pack(pady=10)

        self.submit_button = tk.Button(
            controls, text="Submit ranking", command=self.submit, state="disabled"
        )
        self.submit_button.pack(side="left", padx=5)

        self.next_button = tk.Button(
            controls, text="Next sample", command=self.new_sample, state="disabled"
        )
        self.next_button.pack(side="left", padx=5)

        tk.Button(controls, text="Exit", command=root.destroy).pack(side="left", padx=5)

        self.update_overall()
        self.new_sample()

    def load_ranking(self):
        try:
            with open(self.ranking_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                data = json.load(f)
            return data.get("scores", {}), data.get("shows", {})
        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
            return {}, {}

    def save_ranking(self):
        with open(self.ranking_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump({"scores": self.scores, "shows": self.shows}, f, indent=2)

    def update_overall(self):
        ranked = sorted(
            self.files,
            key=lambda name: self.scores[name] / self.shows[name]
            if self.shows[name] else 0,
            reverse=True,
        )
        lines = ["Current ranking (average points per appearance):"]
        for i, name in enumerate(ranked[:10], 1):
            average = self.scores[name] / self.shows[name] if self.shows[name] else 0
            lines.append(f"{i}. {name} — {average:.2f}")
        self.overall_label.config(text="\n".join(lines))

    def new_sample(self):
        self.selection = []
        self.photo_refs = []
        self.selection_label.config(text="Selected order: (none)")
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_button.config(state="disabled")

        for widget in self.images_frame.winfo_children():
            widget.destroy()

        self.sample = random.sample(self.files, 4)
        for name in self.sample:
            path = os.path.join(self.folder, name)
            with Image.open(path) as image:
                image.thumbnail((220, 220))
                photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(image.copy())

            self.photo_refs.append(photo)
            button = tk.Button(
                self.images_frame,
                image=photo,
                text=name,
                compound="top",
                wraplength=220,
                command=lambda item=name: self.choose(item),
            )
            button.pack(side="left", padx=8, pady=10, expand=True)

    def choose(self, name):
        if name in self.selection:
            return
        self.selection.append(name)
        self.selection_label.config(
            text="Selected order: " + " → ".join(self.selection)
        )
        if len(self.selection) == 4:
            self.submit_button.config(state="normal")

    def submit(self):
        # First choice gets 4 points; last choice gets 1.
        for position, name in enumerate(self.selection):
            self.scores[name] += 4 - position
            self.shows[name] += 1

        try:
            self.save_ranking()
        except OSError as error:
            messagebox.showerror("Save error", str(error))
            return

        self.update_overall()
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_button.config(state="normal")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    root = tk.Tk()
    root.withdraw()
    folder = filedialog.askdirectory(title="Choose a folder of images")
    if folder:
        root.deiconify()
        ImageRanker(root, folder)
    else:
        root.destroy()
    root.mainloop()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Image Ranking GUI

– On startup, a file dialog asks you to choose a directory.
– All images (with extensions .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif) in that directory
  are added as items to rank.
– The program attempts to load a ranking file ("ranking.json") from the directory.
  If it’s not there, a fresh ranking (score zero for each image filename) is created.
– In each “round” 4 images are randomly sampled. They appear as clickable buttons.
  Click them in order (best first, worst last). The selected order appears at the top.
– When all 4 have been chosen, the “Submit Ranking” button is enabled.
  Points are assigned as follows:
      Best image: +4, Second: +3, Third: +2, Fourth: +1.
– The overall ranking (sorted by cumulative score) is updated on the GUI.
– Click “Next Round” to start a new round.
– On exit the ranking file is saved back to disk.
"""

import os, sys, json, random
from tkinter import Tk, Button, Label, Frame, LEFT, RIGHT, BOTH, filedialog, messagebox, TOP, X
from PIL import Image, ImageTk

# Global variables
RANKING_FILENAME = "ranking.json"  # stored in the chosen image directory

class ImageRankingApp:
    def __init__(self, root):
        self.root = root
        self.root.title("Image Ranking")

        # Ask user for a directory containing images.
        self.image_dir = filedialog.askdirectory(title="Select Directory of Images")
        if not self.image_dir:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "No directory selected. Exiting.")
            self.root.destroy()
            sys.exit(1)

        # Gather image file names (filter extensions)
        self.valid_ext = (".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif")
        self.image_files = [f for f in os.listdir(self.image_dir) if f.lower().endswith(self.valid_ext)]
        if len(self.image_files) < 4:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "Need at least 4 images in the directory!")
            self.root.destroy()
            sys.exit(1)

        # Load or initialize cumulative ranking.
        self.ranking_path = os.path.join(self.image_dir, RANKING_FILENAME)
        self.ranking = {}  # image filename -> score
        if os.path.exists(self.ranking_path):
            try:
                with open(self.ranking_path, "r") as f:
                    self.ranking = json.load(f)
            except Exception as e:
                messagebox.showwarning("Warning", "Error loading ranking file. Starting fresh.")
                self.ranking = {}
        # initialize missing images to 0 points
        for img in self.image_files:
            if img not in self.ranking:
                self.ranking[img] = 0

        # These variables hold the current round's state.
        self.current_round_images = []  # list of 4 selected filenames for this round
        self.current_image_buttons = {}  # key: image filename, value: its button widget
        self.button_images = {}  # keep references to PhotoImage objects
        self.selection_order = []  # image filenames chosen in order

        # Create frames for overall ranking, round ranking and control buttons.
        self.create_widgets()
        self.new_round()


    def create_widgets(self):
        # Overall ranking display (top)
        self.overall_frame = Frame(self.root)
        self.overall_frame.pack(fill=X, padx=10, pady=5)
        self.overall_label = Label(self.overall_frame, text="Cumulative Overall Ranking (Name: Score):", font=("Arial", 12, "bold"))
        self.overall_label.pack(anchor="w")
        self.overall_ranking_text = Label(self.overall_frame, text="", justify=LEFT, font=("Arial", 10))
        self.overall_ranking_text.pack(anchor="w")
        self.update_overall_ranking_display()

        # Current round instructions and display (middle)
        self.round_frame = Frame(self.root)
        self.round_frame.pack(fill=BOTH, padx=10, pady=5)
        self.round_instr_label = Label(self.round_frame, text="Round ranking: Click images in order (best to worst):", font=("Arial", 12))
        self.round_instr_label.pack(anchor="w")
        self.selection_status_label = Label(self.round_frame, text="Your selection order: (none)", font=("Arial", 10))
        self.selection_status_label.pack(anchor="w", pady=(0,5))

        self.images_frame = Frame(self.round_frame)
        self.images_frame.pack()

        # Control buttons (bottom)
        self.button_frame = Frame(self.root)
        self.button_frame.pack(pady=10)
        self.submit_button = Button(self.button_frame, text="Submit Ranking", state="disabled", command=self.submit_ranking)
        self.submit_button.pack(side=LEFT, padx=5)
        self.clear_button = Button(self.button_frame, text="Clear Selection", command=self.clear_round)
        self.clear_button.pack(side=LEFT, padx=5)
        self.next_round_button = Button(self.button_frame, text="Next Round", command=self.new_round, state="disabled")
        self.next_round_button.pack(side=LEFT, padx=5)
        self.exit_button = Button(self.button_frame, text="Exit", command=self.on_exit)
        self.exit_button.pack(side=LEFT, padx=5)


    def update_overall_ranking_display(self):
        # Sort by descending score and format the display text.
        sorted_items = sorted(self.ranking.items(), key=lambda item: item[1], reverse=True)
        text_lines = []
        for name, score in sorted_items:
            text_lines.append(f"{name}: {score}")
        self.overall_ranking_text.config(text="\n".join(text_lines))


    def clear_round_interface(self):
        # Destroy existing image buttons in the round
        for widget in self.images_frame.winfo_children():
            widget.destroy()
        self.current_image_buttons = {}
        self.button_images = {}


    def new_round(self):
        # Only allow starting a new round if no active selection or submit already done.
        self.next_round_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.selection_order = []
        self.selection_status_label.config(text="Your selection order: (none)")
        # Clear existing buttons if any.
        self.clear_round_interface()
        # Pick random 4 images from our image list.
        self.current_round_images = random.sample(self.image_files, 4)
        # Create buttons for each image.
        # We display them side-by-side.
        for img_file in self.current_round_images:
            img_path = os.path.join(self.image_dir, img_file)
            # Open image using PIL and resize to a suitable thumbnail (say, 150px wide)
            try:
                im = Image.open(img_path)
                im.thumbnail((150,150))
                photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(im)
            except Exception as e:
                messagebox.showerror("Error", f"Could not load image {img_path}.\n{str(e)}")
                continue

            btn = Button(self.images_frame, image=photo, command=lambda f=img_file: self.image_clicked(f))
            btn.pack(side=LEFT, padx=5, pady=5)
            self.current_image_buttons[img_file] = btn
            self.button_images[img_file] = photo  # keep a reference so image is not garbage collected
        # Enable/disable buttons as needed.
        self.clear_button.config(state="normal")


    def image_clicked(self, img_file):
        # Prevent selecting the same image twice in the round.
        if img_file in self.selection_order:
            return

        self.selection_order.append(img_file)
        # Optionally, disable the button so it cannot be clicked again.
        if img_file in self.current_image_buttons:
            self.current_image_buttons[img_file].config(state="disabled")

        # Update the status label.
        self.selection_status_label.config(text=f"Your selection order: {self.selection_order}")
        # When 4 images are selected, enable submitting.
        if len(self.selection_order) == 4:
            self.submit_button.config(state="normal")


    def clear_round(self):
        self.selection_order = []
        self.selection_status_label.config(text="Your selection order: (none)")
        # re-enable all image buttons.
        for btn in self.current_image_buttons.values():
            btn.config(state="normal")
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_round_button.config(state="disabled")


    def submit_ranking(self):
        # Points to add by order: best gets 4, then 3, 2, 1.
        points_assignment = [4, 3, 2, 1]
        for order, img_file in enumerate(self.selection_order):
            self.ranking[img_file] = self.ranking.get(img_file, 0) + points_assignment[order]

        # Save new cumulative ranking to file.
        try:
            with open(self.ranking_path, "w") as f:
                json.dump(self.ranking, f, indent=2)
        except Exception as e:
            messagebox.showwarning("Save Warning", f"Could not save ranking to file.\n{str(e)}")

        # Update the overall ranking display.
        self.update_overall_ranking_display()
        self.submit_button.config(state="disabled")
        self.next_round_button.config(state="normal")
        # Also disable clear button so the round is done.
        self.clear_button.config(state="disabled")
        messagebox.showinfo("Ranking Submitted", "Your ranking for this round has been submitted.")


    def on_exit(self):
        # Save ranking on exit.
        try:
            with open(self.ranking_path, "w") as f:
                json.dump(self.ranking, f, indent=2)
        except Exception as e:
            messagebox.showwarning("Save Warning", f"Could not save ranking to file on exit.\n{str(e)}")
        self.root.destroy()


def main():
    root = Tk()
    app = ImageRankingApp(root)
    root.mainloop()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
